import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace TwoColorMatching

noncomputable section

def ascendingJacobian (m : Nat) (g x : Fin m → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ :=
  fun j p => -(g p) * x p ^ j.val / (j.val.factorial : ℝ)

def endpointJacobian (m : Nat) (g x : Fin m → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ :=
  (ascendingJacobian m g x).submatrix Fin.rev id

theorem ascending_det (m : Nat) (g x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    (ascendingJacobian m g x).det =
      (∏ j : Fin m, (j.val.factorial : ℝ)⁻¹) *
      (∏ p : Fin m, -(g p)) *
      (∏ i : Fin m, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (x j - x i)) := by
  let B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ :=
    Matrix.of fun j p => -(g p) * (Matrix.vandermonde x).transpose j p
  have h : ascendingJacobian m g x =
      Matrix.of (fun j p => (j.val.factorial : ℝ)⁻¹ * B j p) := by
    ext j p
    simp [ascendingJacobian, B, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]
  have hB : B.det = (∏ p : Fin m, -(g p)) * (Matrix.vandermonde x).transpose.det :=
    Matrix.det_mul_row (fun p => -(g p)) (Matrix.vandermonde x).transpose
  rw [h, Matrix.det_mul_column, hB, Matrix.det_transpose, Matrix.det_vandermonde]
  ring

theorem endpoint_abs_det (m : Nat) (g x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    |(endpointJacobian m g x).det| =
      (∏ j : Fin m, (j.val.factorial : ℝ)⁻¹) *
      (∏ p : Fin m, |g p|) *
      (∏ i : Fin m, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, |x j - x i|) := by
  have h :
      |(endpointJacobian m g x).det| = |(ascendingJacobian m g x).det| := by
    exact Matrix.abs_det_submatrix_equiv_equiv
      Fin.revPerm (Equiv.refl (Fin m)) (ascendingJacobian m g x)
  rw [h, ascending_det]
  simp only [abs_mul, Finset.abs_prod, abs_inv, abs_neg, Nat.abs_cast]

variable {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B]

def hiddenIntegral (q : List A → A → NNReal) (project : A → B)
    (test : List B → NNReal) : Nat → List A → NNReal
  | 0, h => test (h.map project)
  | n + 1, h => ∑ a : A, q h a * hiddenIntegral q project test n (h ++ [a])

def referenceIntegral (w : B → NNReal) (test : List B → NNReal) :
    Nat → List B → NNReal
  | 0, h => test h
  | n + 1, h => ∑ b : B, w b * referenceIntegral w test n (h ++ [b])

theorem fiber_implies_test (q : A → NNReal) (project : A → B) (w : B → NNReal)
    (hdom : ∀ b, (∑ a : A, if project a = b then q a else 0) ≤ w b)
    (test : B → NNReal) :
    (∑ a : A, q a * test (project a)) ≤ ∑ b : B, w b * test b := by
  classical
  calc
    (∑ a : A, q a * test (project a)) =
        ∑ b : B, (∑ a : A, if project a = b then q a else 0) * test b := by
      simp only [Finset.sum_mul]
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      simp [ite_mul]
    _ ≤ ∑ b : B, w b * test b := by
      exact Finset.sum_le_sum (fun b _ => mul_le_mul_right' (hdom b) (test b))

theorem adaptive_domination
    (q : List A → A → NNReal) (project : A → B) (w : B → NNReal)
    (hdom : ∀ h (test : B → NNReal),
      (∑ a : A, q h a * test (project a)) ≤ ∑ b : B, w b * test b)
    (test : List B → NNReal) (n : Nat) (h : List A) :
    hiddenIntegral q project test n h ≤ referenceIntegral w test n (h.map project) := by
  induction n generalizing h with
  | zero => exact le_rfl
  | succ n ih =>
      simp only [hiddenIntegral, referenceIntegral]
      calc
        (∑ a : A, q h a * hiddenIntegral q project test n (h ++ [a])) ≤
            ∑ a : A, q h a * referenceIntegral w test n ((h ++ [a]).map project) := by
          exact Finset.sum_le_sum (fun a _ => mul_le_mul_left' (ih (h ++ [a])) (q h a))
        _ = ∑ a : A, q h a * referenceIntegral w test n (h.map project ++ [project a]) := by
          simp only [List.map_append, List.map_cons, List.map_nil]
        _ ≤ ∑ b : B, w b * referenceIntegral w test n (h.map project ++ [b]) :=
          hdom h (fun b => referenceIntegral w test n (h.map project ++ [b]))

theorem adaptive_domination_from_fibers
    (q : List A → A → NNReal) (project : A → B) (w : B → NNReal)
    (hdom : ∀ h b, (∑ a : A, if project a = b then q h a else 0) ≤ w b)
    (test : List B → NNReal) (n : Nat) (h : List A) :
    hiddenIntegral q project test n h ≤ referenceIntegral w test n (h.map project) := by
  apply adaptive_domination q project w _ test n h
  intro past f
  exact fiber_implies_test (q past) project w (hdom past) f

end

end TwoColorMatching

statement_fidelity.text:
# Statement fidelity: finite and algebraic core of two-color matching

`TwoColorMatching.endpoint_abs_det` is universally quantified over every
natural number `m` and arbitrary real vectors `g,x : Fin m -> Real`. Its
matrix has entry

    -g[p] * x[p]^(m-1-j) / (m-1-j)!

in row `j`, column `p`; row reversal is `Fin.rev`. The theorem states the
exact absolute determinant, not merely its nonvanishing:

    product_j (j!)^(-1) * product_p |g[p]|
      * product_(i<j) |x[j]-x[i]|.

For the manuscript's internal switching variables (numbered from one),
set `g[p]=U[p+1]-U[p]` and `x[p]=s-s[p]`. Then
`x[j]-x[i]=s[i]-s[j]`. Adjoining the final-time coordinate adds a unit
block and leaves this absolute determinant unchanged. No ordering of the
switching times is assumed. The zero-dimensional case also compiles.
`ascending_det` supplies the signed identity before row reversal.

`TwoColorMatching.adaptive_domination_from_fibers` is a separate finite
hidden-history theorem. `A` is any finite hidden-outcome type and `B` any
finite displayed-outcome type. The kernel `q` can depend on the complete
list of past hidden outcomes. It need not have total mass one, so killed
or subprobability kernels are included. `project : A -> B` reveals only
the displayed data. The same nonnegative reference weight `w` is used at
every history. The hypothesis bounds the total `q`-weight in each fiber
of `project` by `w[b]`. For every natural path length, every initial
hidden history, and every nonnegative test of the displayed history, the
theorem bounds the actual recursive hidden integral by the recursive
product-reference integral. There is no conditioning on final survival
and no independence hypothesis on `q`.

`fiber_implies_test` and `adaptive_domination` give the fiber-to-test
translation and the backward-iteration proof. Nonnegative reals are
used so the kernel/test positivity hypotheses are intrinsic.

These are precisely algebraic and finite-kernel components of
`a02:endpoint-jacobian` and the backward iteration following
`a02:full-past-kernel`, respectively. The compiler does **not** verify the
existence of the common control measure in the manuscript's continuous
experiment, Taylor errors, entropy selection, successful-path mass,
change of variables, target volumes, the scale limits, or the Kakeya
theorems. Those are proved in `../report.md` and require independent
mathematical review. In particular this source must not be recorded as
a formal proof of the complete matching lemma.
